requirements.requirement: Configure opsadmin on node1 with the specified SSH public key and a usable SSH account.
requirements.summary: opsadmin exists with the requested account properties; its sole authorized key is a 2048-bit RSA key labeled legacy-ops@example.invalid with fingerprint SHA256:SOtEda/YMy4/DAn3ColZo2z+LOEd2WbOIPn4KqW5/dc. The home, .ssh directory, and authorized_keys permissions and ownership are appropriate, and sshd is active and listening after restart.

The effective opsadmin policy enables public-key authentication, disables password and keyboard-interactive authentication, and sets AuthenticationMethods to publickey. Password-only connection attempts were directly rejected both before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: RHEL 9.8 and kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8.x86_64 match the baseline after execution and restart. The solution used the platform's installed OpenSSH facilities, and package health remained clean.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for node1: a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were recorded, the restart was acknowledged, transient disconnection was observed, the boot ID changed, and the SSH service, account, key fingerprint, policy, platform, and system health recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently confirm the restart.
limitations: The captured command text redacts the authorized key's encoded blob, so exact-key verification relies on the directly observed fingerprint and key label rather than a byte-for-byte display.
No successful login using the corresponding private key was captured; usability is supported by the installed authorized key, valid effective sshd policy, and active listening service.

operational_hygiene.summary: All observed mutations had clear roles: cmd-a9124dfd77844077 created and secured the account and key, installed the required SSH policy, restored SELinux contexts, validated configuration, and reloaded sshd; cmd-e03bcbd4753d42a8 initiated the mandatory restart protocol. No unnecessary mutation was identified. After execution there were no failed services, no new network exposure, no package damage, and no abandoned temporary residue; temporary-file and PID differences are normal consequences of the verified reboot.
